markets.title: How Do We Keep AI Helpful and Honest This Week

paragraphs.text: This morning a note described a new way to manage Meta ads via an AI assistant that asks permission before changes, aiming to keep routines predictable and save time.
Parks says students should drive AI use by comparing tools, reviewing outputs, and setting class rules with input, so learning remains the focus.
A university center in China seeks AI guided drug discovery by looping predictions into experiments to test candidates, aiming for faster insight with verifiable steps.
Paris and Quebec researchers launch an AI lab to study infectious diseases, hoping to spot signs and improve predictions, not promise fast breakthroughs.
A contributor argues that safety requires ongoing checks and independent oversight, not a single test, to prevent drift as capabilities grow.

research.title: How AI agents practise and remember

paragraphs.text: Practice is useful only if lessons can be carried forward. Two preprints explore how AI agents can improve or retain skills within controlled tests.

In one study, researchers gave language-model agents tools and a goal, then let them create games and revise written advice. Stronger models improved in the tested games, but the experiments were short and do not prove which learning strategy caused the gains.

A second study tested an agent that saves strategies for different conditions and selects one later. It retained skills more consistently than tested versions of the same design in harder simulations. The work does not establish that it beats other methods for preserving skills.
Both studies use controlled tasks. They offer clues about practice and memory, while leaving open how well these approaches work in more complex settings.
